what: Australian man dies after falling down ravine on hike to Machu Picchu

clean_source_blocks.text: An Australian man has died after falling down a ravine while walking on the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu in Peru, local authorities have said. Members of the High Mountain Rescue Unit in the city of Cusco found the body of Matthew Cameron Paton, 53, on Thursday, about 300m (984ft) down a steep slope near the "50 Gradas" section of the trail. On Wednesday, Paton - who arrived in Cusco about 12 days ago with his wife - had been reported missing after he fell through a broken railing as he was hiking the famous Peruvian mountain trail with a group of tourists and a guide, police said. Authorities will investigate the cause of the fall and Paton's body is expected to be transferred to a nearby town.

The man died after falling down a ravine on the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu An Australian man has died after falling down a ravine while walking on the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu in Peru, local authorities have said. Members of the High Mountain Rescue Unit in the city of Cusco found the body of Matthew Cameron Paton, 53, on Thursday, about 300m (984ft) down an abyss near the "50 Gradas" section of the trail. On Wednesday, Paton - who arrived in Cusco about 12 days ago with his wife - had been reported missing after he fell through a broken railing as he was hiking the famous Peruvian mountain trail with a group of tourists and a guide, police said.

Matthew Paton was walking along the Inca Trail when he died. Photos: Flickr / Victorian Police An Australian policeman has died after falling several hundred metres into an abyss while walking with a group of tourists and a guide on the Inca Trail in Peru. The accident occurred on Wednesday afternoon (local time) while the hikers were on their way to the World Heritage-listed site of Machu Picchu. Matthew Paton – a 52-year-old Victorian Police sergeant – had reportedly arrived in the Peruvian city of Cusco 12 days earlier. Cusco Police Region Chief, General Virgilio Velasquez, told Peruvian news agency Andina that Paton appeared to have tripped while crossing a wooden bridge. “He likely tried to hold onto the wooden railing, but it gave way and he slipped into the abyss along with it,” he said.
The body of Matthew Cameron Paton, 53, was found on Thursday, about 300m down a steep slope.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
An Australian man has died after falling down a ravine while walking on the Inca Trail to Machu Picchu in Peru, local authorities have said.

Members of the High Mountain Rescue Unit in the city of Cusco found the body of Matthew Cameron Paton, 53, on Thursday, about 300m (984ft) down a steep slope near the "50 Gradas" section of the trail.

On Wednesday, Paton - who arrived in Cusco about 12 days ago with his wife - had been reported missing after he fell through a broken railing as he was hiking the famous Peruvian mountain trail with a group of tourists and a guide, police said.

Authorities will investigate the cause of the fall and Paton's body is expected to be transferred to a nearby town.

Cusco Police Region Chief General Virgilio Velasquez said search and rescue operations were launched on Wednesday after he received reports of the missing man.

"We have information indicating that he apparently tripped while crossing a wooden bridge and he likely tried to hold onto the wooden railing," Velasquez said, according to Peruvian news outlet Andina.

"But it gave way and he slipped into the abyss along with it. Unfortunately, he fell down the ravine," Velasquez added.

In a statement, a spokesman for the Police Association of Victoria (TPAV) said its staff and members were shocked and saddened by "the loss of one of our members in a tragic accident overseas".

"Matt's contribution to policing, through both his role in training police and as a TPAV Assistant Delegate, was representative of the care and concern he had for his colleagues and his want to give back to policing," the association said.

A spokesperson for Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said it was providing consular assistance to the family of a citizen who had died in Peru.

"We send our deepest condolences to the family at this difficult time," the spokesperson said.

---

payload.title: Australialaismies kuoli pudottuaan rotkoon Machu Picchun reitillä
payload.summary: Matthew Cameron Paton löydettiin kuolleena Inkapolun varrelta Perussa sen jälkeen, kun hän oli kadonnut vaelluksella kohti Machu Picchua. Paikallisviranomaisten mukaan ruumis löytyi noin 300 metrin syvyydestä jyrkästä rinteestä.
payload.content:
Australialainen Matthew Cameron Paton, 53, on kuollut pudottuaan rotkoon Inkapolulla Perussa matkalla kohti Machu Picchua. Paikallisviranomaisten mukaan Cuscon kaupungin korkean vuoriston pelastusyksikkö löysi hänen ruumiinsa torstaina noin 300 metrin syvyydestä jyrkästä rinteestä lähellä reitin 50 Gradas -osuutta.

## Mies katosi vaelluksella

Paton oli ilmoitettu kadonneeksi keskiviikkona sen jälkeen, kun hän oli pudonnut vaelluksen aikana. Poliisin mukaan hän oli liikkeellä turistiryhmän ja oppaan kanssa kuuluisalla perulaisella vuoristoreitillä, joka johtaa Machu Picchulle.

Lähteiden mukaan Paton oli saapunut Cuscoon vaimonsa kanssa noin 12 päivää ennen onnettomuutta. Tapaus sattui keskiviikkona iltapäivällä paikallista aikaa, kun vaeltajat olivat matkalla kohti maailmanperintökohteena tunnettua Machu Picchua.

## Kaiteen pettäminen mukana selvityksessä

Viranomaisten alustavien tietojen mukaan Paton putosi rikkoutuneen kaiteen läpi. Cuscon poliisialueen johtaja, kenraali Virgilio Velasquez, kertoi perulaiselle Andina-uutistoimistolle, että Paton näyttää kompastuneen puista siltaa ylittäessään.

Velasquezin mukaan Paton saattoi yrittää tarttua puiseen kaiteeseen, mutta kaide petti ja hän putosi sen mukana rotkoon. Poliisi ei ole vielä vahvistanut tapahtumien tarkkaa kulkua lopullisesti, ja putoamisen syytä selvitetään.

## Ruumis löydettiin vaikeasta maastosta

Pelastajat löysivät Patonin ruumiin torstaina noin 300 metriä alempaa jyrkästä rinteestä tai rotkosta. Lähteissä kuvataan putoamista useiden satojen metrien matkaksi, ja löytöpaikka sijoittui lähelle 50 Gradas -nimellä tunnettua osaa Inkapolusta.

Paikallisviranomaisten mukaan Patonin ruumis on määrä siirtää läheiseen kaupunkiin jatkotoimia varten. Tapausta tutkitaan edelleen Perussa.
summary_bullets: Australialainen Matthew Cameron Paton kuoli pudottuaan rotkoon Inkapolulla Perussa.
Pelastajat löysivät hänen ruumiinsa torstaina noin 300 metrin syvyydestä jyrkästä rinteestä.
Viranomaiset selvittävät, miten putoaminen tapahtui ja mikä rikkoutuneen kaiteen osuus oli onnettomuudessa.
